description: The one store whose data wins when copies disagree. Caches, search indexes and vector stores are rebuilt from it.
Storing each fact once and linking rows by keys, so an update touches one place. Denormalization copies data to make reads cheaper.
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability: the guarantees of a database transaction.
A cluster of data read and written as a unit (an order with its lines). Document stores keep one aggregate per document.
Replicas converge over time; a read right after a write may return the old value.
An array of floats that represents meaning. Vector databases find the nearest embeddings for similarity search and RAG.
